about.title: About Me
introduction: I'm Rajesh Kumar, a product design lead and UI/UX architect with over 20 years in enterprise and telecom software. For 13+ years at Nokia I have shaped how complex network operations tools look and work — and I bridge design strategy and production-grade code, so what gets designed is also performant, accessible and built to scale.

Today, as Frontend Architect, I set the UX and front-end direction for a multi-application network automation platform and its related field-operations and low-code integration products. I own the design system — design tokens, reusable components and UI standards — that brings five operations applications onto one consistent interface with light and dark themes, and I mentor designers and developers, including introducing AI coding assistants to the team.

I specialise in data-dense interfaces where clarity matters: dashboards and cockpit screens that show operators only what needs action, and human-in-the-loop AI patterns where automated, in-review and approved actions are always visible and a person can always override. Earlier, I took Nokia's intranet portal and in-house tools from concept to delivery for 2,500+ users, cutting effort booking and cost recharge work by 90%.

My path started in print and web — graphic design, web templates and brand campaigns — which still shapes how I think about visual craft, alongside formal training in usability (Certified Usability Analyst) and current certifications in UX design and AI development.

principles.title: Users First, Always
principles.description: Every design decision starts with deep user understanding. I validate assumptions through research and testing, never guesswork.

principles.title: Systems Over Screens
principles.description: I design scalable systems, not just interfaces. Components, patterns, and principles that grow with your product and team.

principles.title: Outcomes Over Output
principles.description: Beautiful interfaces are table stakes. I measure success through user outcomes, business KPIs, and measurable impact.

principles.title: Design for Engineering
principles.description: My code background informs every design. I create feasible, performant solutions that engineers love to build.

principles.title: Continuous Learning
principles.description: Technology evolves rapidly. I stay current with emerging patterns, tools, and best practices to deliver modern solutions.

globalCollaboration.title: Global Collaboration
globalCollaboration.description: Most of my work is shaped with people in other time zones. I partner with product, architecture and engineering stakeholders across four countries to turn operations use cases into shipped UI — keeping everyone looking at the same sketch, prototype and screen as the work moves forward.

steps.title: Understand the use case
steps.description: Workshops with product owners and domain experts to map the real operations workflow and who acts at each step.

steps.title: Sketch & prototype
steps.description: Quick sketches, then clickable prototypes that remote stakeholders can try and comment on asynchronously across time zones.

steps.title: Align & decide
steps.description: Reviews with product, architecture and engineering so design, feasibility and priorities are agreed before build.

steps.title: Ship & support
steps.description: Production Angular/React code on the shared design system, carried through testing and customer acceptance (UAT).
